research.dots_2026: 2026 median 3.8% (vs 3.625% current midpoint and 3.4% in March) = ~1 HIKE implied for rest of 2026, NOT cuts. Dot distribution: 9 of 18 above midpoint (favor a hike), 8 at midpoint (hold), 1 below (cut). 2027 median 3.6% (vs 3.1% in March), 2028 median 3.4%, longer run 3.1%. The dot plot flipped from a prior cut bias to a hike bias. Chair Warsh did NOT submit a dot ("I did not submit a dot for me").
research.warsh_presser_tone: HAWKISH (price-stability-first, no forward guidance). Key quotes: "members of the FOMC are unambiguous and unanimous: This Committee will deliver price stability." On forward guidance: "Absent, also, is so-called 'forward guidance,' which we agreed was not well-suited to the current policy conjuncture." On the hawkish board / no cut discussed: "There was one proposal on the table. There was no discussion of any other proposals... The group was unanimous and unambiguous on it." Revamped the statement to ~130 words ("a bit shorter, a bit simpler—and it dispenses with some older language"), declined to submit his own SEP dot, and announced five task forces (communications, balance sheet, data, productivity/jobs, inflation frameworks).

verdict.actual_decision: HOLD — no change. The FOMC voted 12-0 to MAINTAIN the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent (3.50%-3.75%), unchanged for the 4th consecutive meeting. This was Chair Kevin Warsh's first meeting. It was a HOLD-WITH-HAWKISH-DOTS, NOT a hike: the SEP dot plot flipped to a hike-leaning median (end-2026 median rose to 3.8% from 3.4% in March; 9 of 18 officials now project at least one hike by year-end). The 'Fed HIKED' claim is a misread of the dot-plot flip ('Dot Plot Flips to a Hike' headlines) as an actual policy-rate increase. Verified against the primary FOMC statement (federalreserve.gov), which reads verbatim: 'The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.' No rate change occurred.
verdict.ten_year_move_6_17_to_6_19_bps: -3 bps (DOWN). DGS10 (FRED primary): 6/17 close 4.49% -> 6/18 close 4.46% = -3 bps. 6/19/2026 is Juneteenth, a SIFMA-recommended FULL U.S. bond-market close, so there is NO 10Y print on 6/19 — the last print in the window is 6/18. From the 6/17 close through 6/19, the 10Y FELL ~3 bps. The 'decision-day' spike was only +6 bps (6/16 4.43% -> 6/17 4.49%), which then partly retraced. PREDICTION RESOLUTION: '10Y +10bps within 2 sessions' from the 6/17 close = MISS (10Y fell, did not rise; the real move was the 2Y front-end +15 bps to 4.20%, the biggest Fed-day jump since Mar 2008).
verdict.correction: No correction to the first-pass research — it was accurate. First-pass already said HOLD (12-0, 3.50%-3.75% unchanged), and its FRED 10Y figures (4.43 -> 4.49 -> 4.46) and 2Y figures (4.05 -> 4.20 -> 4.19) match the primary data exactly. The only refinement: the 'stunning HIKE' claim under verification is FALSE/debunked — it conflates the hawkish dot-plot flip (median end-2026 to 3.8%) with an actual rate hike. The Fed held; the dots flipped. Also confirm: the '+10bps in 2 sessions' 10Y prediction MISSED (10Y net -3bps over the window because 6/19 is a Juneteenth bond holiday with no print and 6/18 retraced).

boj.decision: HIKE — BOJ raised the policy rate (uncollateralized overnight call rate) by 25bp to around 1.0%, the highest level since 1995. Vote 7-1; Asada Toichiro dissented (favoring a hold on Middle East downside risks). Complementary deposit facility rate set to 1.0%, basic loan rate 1.25%, effective June 17, 2026. Forward guidance retained the tightening bias ("will continue to raise the policy interest rate").
boj.usdjpy_reaction: Yen briefly firmed on the announcement then reversed/stayed weak; USD/JPY settled ~160.2-160.3 (Nikkei reported yen ~160.22). No disorderly move. Intervention risk flagged by analysts/MUFG at the 161-162 zone; the yen's failure to strengthen kept pressure on authorities. Nikkei 225 rose ~0.5-1%; 10Y JGB yield +3bp to ~2.615%.
boj.ueda_status: ABSENT — hospitalized. Governor Kazuo Ueda was hospitalized on June 10, 2026 (reported infected cyst; ~two-week stay) and missed the June 15-16 meeting — the first time a BOJ governor missed a policy meeting since the current arrangement began (1998). He submitted a written policy view but did not vote (recorded as "Absent: UEDA Kazuo" in the BOJ statement). Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino presided over/chaired the meeting; Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida hosted the post-meeting press conference.
boj.vol_outcome: VOL CRUSH / muted — the ~90%-priced, well-telegraphed hike produced no August-2024-style carry-trade unwind spike. Analysts (MUFG, investingLive) judged a disorderly unwind unlikely because the move was extensively communicated and largely anticipated; volatility expected to stay subdued through summer, with renewed carry appetite seen capable of pushing USD/JPY above 160.70. Realized reaction was contained, not a carry-unwind dislocation.
boj.one_line: BOJ hiked 25bp to ~1.0% on June 16, 2026 (7-1, Asada dissent) with Ueda hospitalized and absent — Himino chaired, Uchida ran the presser; the well-telegraphed move produced a vol crush (USD/JPY held ~160.2-160.3, no carry unwind) with intervention risk flagged at 161-162.

releases.name: FOMC decision + SEP + Warsh press conference (June 2026)
releases.actual: Held funds rate 3.50-3.75% (12-0 unanimous). SEP turned hawkish: 2026 PCE raised to 3.6% (core 3.3%), GDP cut to 2.2%, median 2026 funds rate ~3.8%; dot plot flipped from a cut to a possible HIKE — 9 of 18 officials project higher rates by year-end (6 see two 25bp hikes). Warsh (first meeting as Chair) abstained from submitting a dot, dropped forward guidance, cited Middle East conflict uncertainty + elevated inflation.
releases.consensus: Hold was fully priced; market expected a less hawkish dot plot
releases.reaction: Risk-off. S&P 500 -1.21% to 7,420.10; Dow -0.98% (-507 pts); Nasdaq -1.34% to 26,021.66. Treasury yields surged — 2Y +16bp to ~4.22%. Reaction attributed largely to the hawkish dot-plot repricing (Sahm).

today_tape.today_driver: PRIMARY CATALYST (6/23): A global memory-chip/AI-positioning rout, not the Qatar blast or Hormuz. South Korea's KOSPI had its biggest-ever single-day drop, -9.99% to ~8,204 ("Black Tuesday"), with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both down >12%, triggering KRX circuit breakers. The proximate trigger: reports that SK Hynix would SLOW expansion of AI/HBM memory capacity and refocus on conventional DRAM — read as a crack in the AI hardware demand cycle. Compounding Korea-specific catalysts: fading MSCI developed-market inclusion hopes, fears of unrealized-capital-gains taxation, large-scale National Pension Service (NPS) rebalancing, and regulatory scrutiny of leveraged ETFs tied to Samsung/SK Hynix. This spilled into US memory/AI names: SMH -6.5%, Micron (MU) -~11% (down >12% intraday) into its 6/24 earnings, NVDA -3.2% (~$201.97), TSM -5.2% (~$443), Nasdaq ~-1.4% to -2.3%, SPX ~-0.9% to -1% (~7,395-7,403), VIX 18.89 (+9.3%). The move is framed explicitly as "doubts about the AI trade / overstretched AI valuations," i.e., a positioning unwind in the most crowded longs. SECONDARY/AMPLIFIER: the 6/17 hawkish-FOMC repricing (median 2026 dot raised to 3.8%, 9/18 see a hike, ~75% odds of a Sept hike) keeps the discount-rate headwind live and removes the rate-cut cushion under high-multiple tech — so an AI-demand scare lands on an already-de-risked, higher-yield backdrop. ALTERNATIVE-MANAGER CRACK (ARES -5%, APO -2.7%): these are the high-beta expression of the same risk-off, layered on a STANDING private-credit/AI-displacement vulnerability that has hit alts all year (UBS est. 25-35% of private-credit exposed to AI-disrupted software; redemption-gate/bank-run fears since Feb-Mar 2026). MINOR/NON-DRIVER: Qatar Ras Laffan/Barzan blast (~6/22, 13+ killed) — Qatar said NO impact to LNG exports (Barzan feeds domestic power/water, not export trains); a tail geopolitical-premium item, not today's driver. Iran/Hormuz is a TAILWIND-turned-neutral (6/15 peace deal reopened Hormuz, blockade formally ended 6/18) — it removed the energy-risk premium and is not driving 6/23 risk-off. Month-end/quarter-end rebalancing is a latent flow risk into 6/30 but was not cited as today's catalyst.
today_tape.week_path: SPX path 6/18→6/23 (US sessions): 6/15 (Mon) record close ~7,554 (+1.65%) on US-Iran peace deal + Hormuz reopen. 6/16 (Tue) Dow record, SPX flat-to-soft into FOMC. 6/17 (Wed) FOMC hawkish hold (Warsh's 1st meeting): SPX -1.21% to 7,420.10; Dow -507 to 51,492; Nasdaq -1.34% to 26,021; 10Y +6.9bp to 4.497%. 6/18 (Thu) REBOUND: Russell 2000 +2.12% / Nasdaq up as yields eased and US formally ended the Iran blockade. 6/19 (Fri, Juneteenth — US markets closed). 6/22 (Mon) tech/memory selloff begins overnight, but it's a ROTATION not broad risk-off: SPX only -0.37% to 7,472.79, Dow +0.29% (+148, CAT +~4%), and Russell 2000 closes at a record >3,000 (3,004.40) for the first time ever — yet Alphabet -5%, MSFT -3%, Amazon -4.8%, Meta -2.3%; Micron actually +~7% that day. 6/23 (Tue) the rout goes GLOBAL and broad after KOSPI -9.99%: SPX intraday ~-0.9% to -1% (~7,395-7,403; full-session reads showed up to -1.5% to ~7,353), Nasdaq -1.4% to -2.3% (~25,800), Dow roughly flat/+0.2% (defensive/value bid persists). Net: SPX ~-2% to -2.5% from the 6/15 record (~7,551-7,554) into 6/23 (~7,395), a controlled de-rate concentrated in mega-cap AI/semis with small-caps and value cushioning the tape — classic mechanical-rotation-then-broadening sequence rather than a cascade. Confirm a daily close for the exact 6/23 print.
today_tape.vix_path: VIX path: subdued-to-rising, NOT a panic spike. Through the prior weeks VIX averaged ~17.4 (range ~15.18-23.34 over 5/25-6/23). 6/17 FOMC bumped vol modestly. 6/22 close 17.28 (+2.98%; range 16.49-17.92) — notably calm given the overnight chip wobble, because 6/22 was rotation (small-caps/value up) not broad risk-off. 6/23 the KOSPI crash forced a re-rate: VIX 18.89, +1.61 (+9.3%), with intraday prints ~19 (prompt's +9.7% snapshot is consistent). VVIX +7.6% (vol-of-vol rising) signals demand for convexity/tail hedges, i.e., desks paying up for protection as the AI-positioning unwind broadens. Interpretation: VIX still BELOW the 23-24 vol-control trigger and below the 30 risk-off-regime line — term structure likely still contango/flattening, not backwardated. This is a positioning/de-risking jolt, not yet a systematic-deleveraging cascade. Watch for VIX sustained >23-24 (vol-control selling) and a flip to backwardation as the escalation tell; MU earnings (6/24) is the near-term vol pivot.
today_tape.sector_leaders_laggards: LAGGARDS (6/23): Semiconductors/memory the epicenter — SMH -6.5%, Micron -~11% (>12% intraday), NVDA -3.2%, TSM -5.2%; Korea ADRs/Samsung/SK Hynix -12%. Mega-cap tech/AI broadly: Nasdaq -1.4% to -2.3%; on 6/22 Alphabet -5%, MSFT -3%, Amazon -4.8%, Meta -2.3%. Alternative-asset managers got hit hard as high-beta + private-credit/AI-software-exposure proxy: ARES -5%, APO -2.7% (peers KKR/BX/Blue Owl/TPG in the same complex, vulnerable on the standing private-credit redemption/AI-disruption theme). LEADERS / RELATIVE STRENGTH: Value/cyclicals and small-caps cushioned — Dow roughly flat-to-up (6/22 +0.29% led by Caterpillar ~+4%; 6/23 ~flat/+0.2%), Russell 2000 hit a record >3,000 on 6/22 and showed relative strength into 6/23. The tape is a within-equity rotation OUT of crowded AI/semis/long-duration growth INTO value, defensives, and small-caps — a quality/factor unwind, not indiscriminate selling. Energy a wildcard given Qatar blast headlines but Hormuz reopening capped the oil premium.
today_tape.one_line: 6/23 risk-off is a global memory-chip/AI-positioning unwind (KOSPI -9.99% on SK Hynix's AI-memory capex pullback + Korea-specific MSCI/tax/pension flows), landing on a market already de-risked by the 6/17 hawkish-FOMC dot-plot repricing — semis/mega-cap AI and alt-managers lead lower while value/small-caps cushion; the Qatar LNG blast and Hormuz are tail/neutral, not the driver.

froth.ai_semi_concentration:
PARTIALLY CONFIRMED / MIXED.

SEMICONDUCTOR SUB-CLAIM — CONFIRMED. Semiconductors at a RECORD ~18.8% of S&P 500 market cap (mid-June 2026, "more than triple their share in 2022," and larger than the dot-com/tech-bubble peak) is well-corroborated and traces to Citadel Securities Global Market Intelligence. Citadel framing: "roughly 18 cents of every dollar allocated to the S&P 500 is directed toward semiconductor companies, 33 cents flows into the Mag 7, and nearly 40 cents is concentrated in the index's ten largest holdings" (citadelsecurities.com/news-and-insights/global-market-intelligence). The "2.5x the dot-com peak" multiplier is NOT the exact language used — primary/reputable sources say "more than double" / "larger than during the Dot-Com era" / "more than triple their share in 2022." The 18.8% level is dated June 19, 2026 (coinpedia citing the data). YEAR CONFIRMED 2026.

AI SUB-CLAIM — CORRECTED on both number and attribution. The widely-cited record figure is AI ~45% of S&P 500 market cap, NOT 47%. The 45% figure traces to The Kobeissi Letter ("AI-linked stocks now account for a record 45% of the S&P 500's total market cap," reported Apr 24, 2026) and SEPARATELY to Goldman Sachs ("AI stocks near 45% of S&P 500 weight, Goldman Sachs says," Seeking Alpha). Apollo/Torsten Slok IS a real AI-concentration commentator but his published figures are framed differently — top-10 stocks >40% of index market cap, and "S&P 500 gains since January come entirely from AI + energy" — NOT a clean "47% of market cap" number. So the relay's "AI ~47% (Apollo/Slok)" mis-states the number (45%, not 47%) and mis-attributes the headline market-cap figure (Kobeissi/Goldman, not Apollo). YEAR CONFIRMED 2026.
froth.levered_etf: UNCONFIRMED as stated ($464bn) — and likely a metric/scope mismatch. Could not source a Goldman "record ~$464 billion" leveraged/inverse ETF NET EXPOSURE figure in any reputable wire or primary. What IS confirmed from Goldman (via CNBC, June 3 2026, "Leveraged ETF assets double in two months as investors press AI bet," citing Goldman's Christian Mueller-Glissmann): US leveraged EQUITY ETF net assets ~$84bn at end-May 2026 (up from ~$39bn in April), plus leveraged ETFs on South Korea/Taiwan ~$43.1bn (from ~$17bn) — i.e. assets roughly DOUBLED in two months on the AI trade.
